Plane & Grain – Knockdown furnitureStory
4th Year || Final project || Prof. Sefi Hefetz

A material dialogue

The identity of the collection rests on a deliberate dialogue between two materials, kept visible rather than resolved away.
Every piece is made from just 5mm aluminum and solid oak.

The PlaneAluminum

Sanded aluminum sheet, waxed for a natural finish in a muted, desaturated slate blue-gray. Sharp architectural lines, geometric rigidity, thin profiles.

The GrainOak

Rich, warm oak. Organic permanence, texture, and the structural mass that grounds each piece.

Precision mechanical joinery

Toolless assembly

Aluminum panels slip directly through precision-milled slots in the oak. No tools required.

No adhesives

Structural rigidity comes purely from geometry, friction, and gravity: no screws, fasteners, or wood glue.

Honest construction

Metal tabs stay visible where they punctuate the wood, turning the logic of the joint into a decorative, functional feature.

Plane & Grain – Knockdown furnitureStory
4th Year || Final project || Prof. Sefi Hefetz

Flat-pack & circular

Flat

Ships fully knocked-down, maximizing shipping volume and minimizing transport emissions.

Clean

No permanent glue or fused materials. Aluminum and oak separate cleanly for recycling or repurposing.

Surface

Both materials are sanded to a low grit and finished with wax, so the aluminum ages and matures naturally alongside the oak.

Design Koren Blumberg
Guidance Prof. Sefi Hefetz
Thanks Nitzan Chazut, Alex Belous

3rd Year || “simply a tool” || Nitsan Debbi

simply a tool

mentored by
Nitsan Debbi

Head of Bezalel’s Industrial Design department and senior designer at Naoto Fukasawa

A course that uses “simple” design thinking and rapid development to create multiple tools, then a whole system out of one of them.

The year I took part, the focus was cutlery, and I was ranked best in class.

“simply a tool” – Set
3rd Year || “simply a tool” || Nitsan Debbi

Driven by the ‘finger method’ for measuring soup thickness and the lollipop “icon,” this series uses a revolved cut to define its functional identity. This geometry creates a tactile, shallow bowl for the spoon and a sharp edge for the fork and knife, resulting in a durable, CNC-machined maple set and stainless steel spoon.

“simply a tool” – Dosage
3rd Year || “simply a tool” || Nitsan Debbi

Responding to a measuring spoon brief, I utilized brass for its antibacterial properties to create a specialized tool for health supplement and pill dosages.

The final outcome features two distinct sizes: a compact version for a single dosage, shown here with an Advil, and an elongated model tailored for a double measurement, scaled to standard supplement dimensions.

“simply a tool” – Charred quenelle
3rd Year || “simply a tool” || Nitsan Debbi

A bite inspired by Chef Giuseppe Gasperoni
Based on a brief interview and further research, we were tasked with creating a spoon for Milan Design Week that reflects Chef Gasperoni’s unique philosophy, combining tradition with contemporary innovation.
January 2025

Crafted from maple scrap wood sourced from sap-harvested trees, this gelato spoon is designed to be gently charred in front of guests, imparting a delicate burnt aroma and flavor. The warm material and quenelle shape enhance the gelato experience.

Plastic Data
Mapping

Nordhavn route
12 September 2026

An interactive map of the plastic found along a walking route through Nordhavn, Copenhagen. 51 artifacts were documented across four sites in 39 entries, each photographed and logged by material, colour, wear, texture, and whether it’s reusable or disposable.

Walk the route site by site, spin the wheel for a random find, or regroup the whole collection in Selma’s Sort.

About

I am Koren,I mix a crafty, hands-on approach, 3D modeling, deep research and user-centered thinking to solve real-world problems. With a background in Agile tech teams, I connect design and engineering and keep projects moving smoothly across disciplines.

I’m now pursuing an MSc in Strategic Design & Entrepreneurship, a joint program of the Royal Danish Academy and Copenhagen Business School, and I’m especially interested in the consulting world, where design, strategy and business meet.
